performanceArena._comment: Performance Arena is server-authoritative: clients never read or write this tree directly — all access goes through authenticated API routes using the Admin SDK. Balances, results, rewards, leaderboard entries and fraud flags cannot be edited client-side.

alerts._comment: User price/structure alerts. Phase 11 audit: this path was written by app/api/alerts via the Admin SDK but had NO rule, so with the deny-by-default root every client read was refused. Owner-scoped, never cross-user readable.

monitoring._comment: Setup Memory (MEMORY_PATHS in lib/market-intelligence/memory/repository.ts -> monitoring/setups/$uid). Phase 11 audit: the repository wrote here but no rule existed, so clients were denied while the Admin SDK wrote — setups were invisible on every client. Owner-scoped: a setup is private by default and is never readable by another user.

deviceWorkspace._comment: Phase 11 cross-device workspace. SERVER-AUTHORITATIVE: clients may read their own workspace (so every surface — desktop, PWA, native — sees the same state) but may NEVER write directly. Writes go through /api/mobile/workspace so revision is bumped by the server and validation is enforced. Denying .write here is what makes deterministic conflict resolution possible.

userPreferences._comment: Phase 11 cross-device preferences. Same model as deviceWorkspace: owner-readable, server-only writes via /api/mobile/preferences. Separate from deviceWorkspace so a new device can render in the right theme before the workspace record resolves.

mobileDevices._comment: Phase 11 device registry. Server-only in both directions: it records deviceId, platform, app version and last-seen for admin observability and conflict attribution. Clients must never be able to enumerate or edit another device's record.
